questions.q: What is the primary reason for wearing safety goggles in the science laboratory?
a: To protect the eyes from chemical splashes, flying debris, and heat
To look like a professional scientist
To improve vision under dim laboratory lights
To keep dust away from the face

questions.q: What should you do immediately if a chemical substance splashes into your eyes?
a: Rub your eyes vigorously with dry hands
Rinse eyes continuously at the eyewash station and inform the teacher
Cover your eyes with a clean cloth and wait until class ends
Apply cooking oil to soothe the irritation

questions.q: Which of the following equipment is specifically designed to put out small clothing fires or wrap around someone whose clothes are burning?
a: Fire extinguisher
Sand bucket
Fire blanket
Fume cupboard

questions.q: Why is it strictly forbidden to taste or eat any substance in the science laboratory?
a: Because laboratory chemicals are expensive
Because food is not allowed in school
Because it wastes time during practical lessons
Because chemicals may be toxic, corrosive, or contaminated and cause severe poisoning

questions.q: What is the correct procedure for smelling a chemical substance in the laboratory?
a: Wafting the vapor gently toward your nose with your hand
Placing your nose directly over the open test tube and inhaling deeply
Heating the container strongly and sniffing the smoke
Tasting a small drop on the tip of your tongue first

questions.q: Which of the following symbols on a chemical container indicates that the substance can burn easily and catch fire rapidly?
a: Corrosive symbol
Flammable symbol
Radioactive symbol
Toxic skull and crossbones

questions.q: What is the safest way to dilute an concentrated acid with water?
a: Pour water quickly into the concentrated acid
Add the acid slowly to water while stirring constantly
Mix equal volumes of acid and water at once without stirring
Heat the acid before adding any water

questions.q: What should you do if you break a glass beaker during a practical session?
a: Pick up the large pieces with your bare hands and throw them in the dustbin
Sweep the glass under the table and leave it there
Ignore it and continue working with the remaining equipment
Inform the teacher immediately and use a brush and dustpan to clean up safely

questions.q: Which piece of protective clothing is worn to protect school clothes and skin from harmful chemical spills?
a: Laboratory coat or apron
Woolen sweater
Silk scarf
Heavy winter jacket

questions.q: What does a hazard sign showing a skull and crossbones signify?
a: The substance is highly explosive
The substance is toxic or poisonous
The substance is extremely cold
The substance is a source of electrical power

questions.q: Why must long hair be tied back securely during laboratory experiments involving open flames?
a: To keep students looking neat
To prevent sweat on the forehead
To prevent hair from accidentally catching fire or dipping into chemicals
To make it easier to wear safety goggles

questions.q: Which of the following actions demonstrates good laboratory safety practice?
a: Running around the laboratory to collect apparatus quickly
Tasting unknown chemicals to identify them
Performing unauthorized experiments when the teacher is away
Following all written and verbal instructions given by the teacher

questions.q: Where should chemical waste, such as strong acids or toxic metal solutions, be disposed of?
a: In designated waste containers specified by the teacher
By pouring it into the classroom flower pots
By drinking it to test its strength
By throwing it out of the laboratory window

questions.q: What is the primary function of a fume cupboard in a science laboratory?
a: To store extra glassware and test tubes
To safely remove toxic or noxious gases and vapors away from the user
To heat water to boiling point rapidly
To cool down hot metallic objects

questions.q: How should you heat a liquid in a test tube using a Bunsen burner?
a: Point the mouth of the test tube directly at your lab partner
Hold the test tube completely stationary at the very bottom of the flame
Point the mouth of the test tube away from yourself and others while moving it gently
Seal the test tube tightly with a rubber bung before heating

questions.q: What is the first step you should take if a chemical spills on your skin?
a: Wipe it off with a dry piece of tissue paper
Apply a layer of petroleum jelly immediately
Cover the affected area with a bandage without cleaning
Wash the affected area immediately with plenty of running water and notify the teacher

questions.q: Why are open-toed shoes or sandals prohibited in the science laboratory?
a: To protect feet from spilled chemicals and falling sharp objects
Because they make too much noise on the floor
Because they are not part of the school uniform code
To ensure students can run faster during drills

questions.q: What should be used to handle hot crucibles or evaporating dishes after heating?
a: Bare hands if they look dry
Tongs or heat-resistant gloves
A piece of wet tissue paper
Plastic forceps

questions.q: What does a corrosive hazard symbol indicate about a chemical?
a: It will explode when exposed to air
It causes skin irritation only when licked
It can destroy living tissue and damage metals upon contact
It glows brightly in the dark

questions.q: Why is it important to wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water after every practical lesson?
a: To remove any invisible chemical residues or harmful microorganisms
To cool your hands down after handling glassware
To make your skin smell nice for the next class
To test the quality of the laboratory soap

questions.q: What should you do if the Bunsen burner flame goes out unexpectedly?
a: Turn off the gas tap immediately
Keep the gas tap open and try striking a match near the burner
Throw water onto the burner
Blow into the gas tubing to clear blockages

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of unsafe behavior in the laboratory?
a: Reading instructions carefully before starting an experiment
Horseplay, pushing, or running around the laboratory benches
Keeping your working area clean and tidy
Reporting any cracked glassware to the teacher

questions.q: What is the correct way to test the odor of a gas produced in a test tube?
a: Inhale deeply directly above the open mouth of the test tube
Taste a small amount of the gas
Waft the fumes gently toward your nose with your hand
Seal the test tube and shake it near your face

questions.q: Why must electrical equipment with frayed wires never be used in the laboratory?
a: Because they cost too much money to replace
Because they consume too much electricity
Because they do not match modern laboratory decor
Because they pose a serious risk of electric shock and fire outbreaks

questions.q: What is the main purpose of safety rules in the school laboratory?
a: To prevent accidents, injuries, and ensure a safe working environment
To make practical lessons as difficult as possible
To prevent students from ever using chemicals
To reduce the amount of equipment used in school

questions.q: What type of fire extinguisher is generally used for electrical fires in the laboratory?
a: Water-filled fire extinguisher
Carbon dioxide or dry powder extinguisher
Foam bucket filled with muddy water
Hand-held water hose

questions.q: When should safety goggles be worn during a practical session?
a: Only when writing down observations in your notebook
Only when leaving the laboratory
At all times when working with chemicals, heat, or glassware
Only when the teacher asks you to take a photo

questions.q: What is the correct action to take if your clothing catches fire in the laboratory?
a: Run out of the laboratory as fast as you can to find water
Wave your arms wildly to blow the flames out
Stand completely still and shout for help
Stop, drop, and roll, and have someone cover you with a fire blanket

questions.q: Why should you never return unused chemicals to their original stock bottles?
a: It can contaminate the entire stock bottle with impurities
Stock bottles are always kept locked away
Unused chemicals turn into solids instantly
It is against school administrative policy

questions.q: What should you check before heating a glass test tube with a Bunsen burner?
a: Whether the test tube has any colorful stickers on it
Whether the test tube is dry on the outside and free of cracks
Whether the test tube is filled to the very brim
Whether the test tube is made of ordinary window glass

questions.q: What is the purpose of the yellow luminous flame (safety flame) on a Bunsen burner when it is not actively being used for heating?
a: To heat substances as fast as possible
To produce maximum light in the room
To make the burner easily visible so no one gets burned accidentally
To burn up excess gas in the pipes

questions.q: How should gas cylinders or burners be handled at the end of a practical session?
a: Leave the main gas valve open for the next class
Blow out the flame and leave the gas tap open
Disconnect all rubber tubing with bare hands
Turn off the gas supply valves securely at the bench and main source

questions.q: Which of the following is considered personal protective equipment (PPE) in a science lab?
a: Safety goggles, lab coat, and protective gloves
School backpack and pencil case
Sports jersey and running sneakers
Leather belt and wrist watch

questions.q: What should you do if you feel dizzy or unwell after inhaling fumes in the laboratory?
a: Continue working until the lesson finishes
Move immediately to fresh air outside the laboratory and inform the teacher
Lie down flat on the laboratory floor
Drink a cup of cold water from the sink

questions.q: Why are walkways and aisles in the laboratory required to be kept clear of bags and stools?
a: To make the room look spacious for visitors
To allow students to dance during breaks
To prevent tripping hazards and allow quick evacuation during emergencies
To keep bags clean and free from dust

questions.q: What should be done with broken or chipped glassware?
a: Glue it back together with school gum and use it again
Hide it in the back of the storage cupboard
Wrap it in old newspaper and give it away
Discard it in a special rigid container designated for broken glass

questions.q: Why is eating or drinking strictly prohibited during a science experiment?
a: Food can easily absorb toxic chemical vapors or become contaminated with poisonous substances
Eating makes students sleepy during lessons
Teachers want to keep all snacks for themselves
Food reacts violently with ordinary laboratory air

questions.q: What is the appropriate response if a small chemical fire starts on a bench top?
a: Throw a bucket of loose sand or use a suitable fire extinguisher, and notify the teacher
Fan the flames with a notebook to blow them out
Pour cooking oil over the fire
Pour concentrated acid onto the fire

questions.q: How should reagent bottles be handled when pouring liquids into test tubes?
a: Hold the label upside down so it gets wet
Place the stopper flat on the dusty floor
Hold the label facing upwards against your palm so drips do not damage the label
Hold the bottle as far away from your body as possible without support

questions.q: What is the key rule regarding unauthorized experiments in the laboratory?
a: They are allowed if you finish your classwork early
They are encouraged if you bring your own ingredients
They can be performed quietly with a partner
They are strictly prohibited because they can lead to serious, uncontrolled accidents
